email.body1:
Eliza, saw HungerRush shipped the Grubhub Marketplace integration and is leaning into AI ordering, now driving nearly twice the conversation of traditional POS.

For sales ops, more inbound usually creates a signal-to-action gap: leads pile up faster than reps can work them, and conversion leaks at the handoff. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up on its own, so every signal gets actioned without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for HungerRush off your hiring and tech-stack data, and accounts showing them progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Eliza, quick follow-up for HungerRush.

Most sales ops teams lose measurable pipeline to slow follow-up and inconsistent data hygiene, not lack of leads. Tightening that motion is usually the fastest lift you can show the number.

Worth 15 minutes? I will walk you through a teardown of your current outbound and three changes I would make. Our best practices alone tend to lift response rates 50 to 70 percent.
email.body3:
Eliza, last bit of proof for HungerRush.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how your reply rate likely compares to other restaurant-tech teams. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Eliza, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If tightening signal-to-action without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. A busy ops calendar is its own kind of full.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your ops motion? I will tailor it to HungerRush either way.
